name: Nethinims
overview: The Nethinims were a distinct group identified in Scripture as servants assigned to assist the Levites in their duties, reflecting a special role within the worship and service structure of Israel (1 Chronicles 9:2). They are listed among those who returned from the Babylonian captivity, indicating their continued presence and function in the restored community of Jerusalem (Ezra 2:43, 2:58, 2:70). Their importance is further underscored by the explicit exemption from taxation granted to them, along with priests, Levites, singers, and porters, highlighting their dedicated service to the house of God (Ezra 7:24).
